model.name: Market / Exchange
model.purpose: Governed context model for an organised market or exchange as a rule-governed facility that brings together, or reports, multiple third-party buying and selling interests and that is identifiable as a place of official listing, place of trade, or trade-reporting facility.
model.scope_statement: This model covers one organised market, exchange, trading platform, market segment, or trade-reporting facility as a format-neutral record of identity, class, operator binding, composition, access rules, trading-state, rulebook references, and register evidence. It records venue-side parameters and references to instruments, members, post-trade infrastructures and authorities. It does not own the lifecycle of those referenced parties, the matching or clearing of individual orders and trades, or competition-law market definition.
in_scope: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code identity at operating and segment level, including MIC type, status, expiry and last-update metadata

Venue and facility class under applicable law and ISO 10383 market category codes, including regulated market, MTF, OTF, ATS, DCM, SEF, recognised market operator, crypto-asset trading platform, and trade-reporting facility
Operator binding via legal entity name and LEI without reproducing legal-entity lifecycle
Whole-part composition of operating market and specialised segments or facilities
Admission-to-trading or listing set as a venue-side register of referenced instruments or contracts
Membership, participant and access-rule parameters, including fair-access and direct-electronic-access conditions stated by the venue
Trading calendar, session model, halt and emergency-state of the venue itself
Pre-trade and post-trade transparency regime applicable to the venue
Rulebook identity, competent-authority binding, and public-register evidence
Place-of-listing versus place-of-trade versus trade-reporting-facility roles
out_of_scope: Individual orders, quotes, trades, positions, allocations and confirmations, including matching-engine execution, best-execution evaluation and trade lifecycle
Financial instruments, contracts, crypto-assets or commodities as products; this model only stores admission or listing bindings
Legal person, partnership or unincorporated association that operates the market, except the LEI and name binding
Central counterparties, central securities depositories, securities settlement systems, payment systems and trade repositories as financial market infrastructures; only venue-side links are kept
Market-abuse, enforcement, disciplinary and supervisory audit-trail records
Competition-law relevant product or geographic market
Informal bilateral OTC dealing that is not a MIC-bearing facility and does not operate a multilateral system
E-commerce catalogue or marketplace platforms that do not bring together multiple third-party trading interests under trading-venue or equivalent rules
Price indices, benchmarks and market-data products as commercial objects
Physical geometry, mass, colour or other material measurements of trading floors

boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 10383 Release 2.0 stores legal entity name and LEI of the organisation that operates the market. This model keeps that binding and operator-role parameters only. Incorporation, control, officers and LEI lifecycle belong to the legal-entity model.

Admission to trading, listing and delisting are venue-side events recorded here as references. Instrument terms, ISIN or other instrument identifiers, and asset lifecycle belong to the instrument or crypto-asset model.
The venue is a place of trade. Order books, executions, confirmations and trade-state machines are not owned here. A reference to a runtime matcher does not grant ownership of execution semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Central counterparty, CSD, SSS, payment system, trade repository
boundary_notes.distinction: CPMI-IOSCO PFMI apply to payment systems, CSDs, SSS, CCPs and trade repositories, not to trading venues as such. MiFID recital 15 excludes CCPs from the OTF definition. This model stores designated clearing, settlement and reporting links only.
Antitrust relevant-market definition is a product-and-geography substitutability construct. It is not the organised exchange or MIC-bearing facility modelled here.

MiFID II Article 4(24) defines trading venue as RM, MTF or OTF only, and Article 4(20) defines an SI as bilateral dealing without operating a multilateral system. ISO 10383 and FIBO nonetheless assign MIC category SINT and treat SI as a market identifier subject. This model may carry an SI MIC binding and the bilateral flag; it must not treat SI as a multilateral trading venue.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Data reporting services provider (APA, ARM, CTP)
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 10383 and FIBO assign MICs to DRSPs as sources of prices and related information. Operating a DRSP is not operating a market. This model may store the MIC binding; DRSP authorisation and tape operations belong to a data-reporting sibling.

Authorisation, designation, core-principle oversight and licence withdrawal are acts of an authority. This model stores the governing authority reference, authorisation status and rule-file identifiers, not the authority's own lifecycle or enforcement case files.
Country, municipality and trading-session times are recorded as venue operating attributes. Canonical location and calendar models remain the masters for geographic and holiday semantics.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: Authoritative identification of a market or exchange and the legal and register classes that distinguish multilateral venues, segments, bilateral MIC-bearing facilities and reporting facilities.
bundles.rationale: ISO 10383 exists specifically to identify exchanges, platforms, markets and trade-reporting facilities. MiFID II, the Exchange Act, the CEA and MiCA then split that identified facility into mutually exclusive regulatory classes whose perimeter is not identical across jurisdictions.

layers.name: Market identifiers
layers.description: MIC allocation, operating versus segment level, names, acronyms and status fields published by the ISO 10383 Registration Authority.

findings.name: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code
findings.description: A market or exchange instance is identified by a four-character alphanumeric MIC randomly allocated by SWIFT as ISO 10383 Registration Authority. The code has no intelligence in any character, cannot be modified once allocated, and is the identifier used as place of official listing, place of trade, or trade-reporting facility.

questions.text: What four-character ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code currently identifies this market, segment or trade-reporting facility?
answer_data: Exactly four A-Z0-9 characters as published in the ISO 10383 MIC list; not a date, LEI, ticker or local surrogate.

questions.text: Is this MIC an operating-level code (OPRT) or a market-segment code (SGMT)?
answer_data: Controlled value OPRT or SGMT from the ISO 10383 Release 2.0 MIC type field.

questions.text: What operating MIC is the parent of this code, and is this record itself the operating MIC?
answer_data: Four-character operating MIC; equal to the MIC when the record is operating-level.

questions.text: What market name-institution description, legal entity name and facility acronym are published for this MIC?
answer_data: Object with market_name (max 255), legal_entity_name (optional max 255) and acronym as carried on the ISO 10383 record.

questions.text: What ISO 10383 status, last-update date and expiry date apply to this MIC, and when did the Registration Authority last publish versus make the change effective?
answer_data: Status in {ACTIVE, UPDATED, EXPIRED}, last_update_date, expiry_date if any, publication_date and modification_implementation_date as RFC 3339 datetimes with seconds and offset.

artifacts.name: ISO 10383 MIC register record

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the MIC together with the publication date and modification implementation date of the ISO 10383 list from which the extract was taken.

layers.name: Venue classes and recognition
layers.description: Regulatory and ISO category classes, plus the multilateral-system test that distinguishes a trading venue from bilateral dealing and from mere data reporting.

findings.name: Venue class and jurisdictional perimeter
findings.description: The same MIC-bearing facility may be a regulated market, MTF, OTF, ATS, DCM, SEF, recognised market operator, crypto-asset trading platform, trade-reporting facility, or an SI/DRSP with a MIC. Classes are jurisdiction-specific alignments, not a single global taxonomy. ISO 10383 market category codes include RMKT, MLTF, OTFS, ATSS, DCMS, SEFS, RMOS, TRFS, SINT, CASP, APPA, ARMS, CTPS, IDQS, NSPD and OTHR.

questions.text: Which ISO 10383 market category code is assigned to this MIC, and is that code semantically empty (NSPD or OTHR)?
answer_data: ISO 10383 market category code such as RMKT, MLTF, OTFS, ATSS, DCMS, SEFS, SINT, TRFS, CASP, APPA, ARMS, CTPS, IDQS, RMOS, NSPD or OTHR.

questions.text: Under the governing legal system, is this facility a trading venue (RM, MTF or OTF), a US national securities exchange, an ATS operating under an exchange exemption, a DCM, a SEF, a MiCA crypto-asset trading platform, a trade-reporting facility, or a systematic internaliser?
answer_data: Object with jurisdiction, legal_class, and whether the class is a MiFID trading venue as defined in Article 4(24).

questions.text: If the MIC category is SINT, APPA, ARMS or CTPS, what evidence shows the facility is not a multilateral trading venue, and which sibling model owns SI quoting or DRSP operations?
answer_data: Boolean not_a_multilateral_trading_venue, conflict_note, and referenced sibling model name.

questions.text: Which foreign or home-register classes are claimed as equivalent or substituted (for example SEF versus OTF, ATS versus MTF), and what primary evidence supports or contradicts that alignment?
answer_data: Array of alignment objects with home_class, foreign_class, evidence_url and conflict_flag.

data_elements.name: ISO 10383 market category code
data_elements.description: Controlled market-category classifier.

data_elements.name: Legal venue class
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction-specific legal class of the facility.

data_elements.name: Is MiFID trading venue
data_elements.description: True only for RM, MTF or OTF.

data_elements.name: Cross-regime class alignments
data_elements.description: Claimed equivalences and conflicts.

artifacts.name: Market category and legal-class assignment
artifacts.description: Record of ISO 10383 category, legal class under each relevant statute, and documented conflicts such as SI-with-MIC versus MiFID trading-venue perimeter.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the MIC plus the jurisdiction and statutory provision under which the legal class is assigned.

findings.name: Multilateral recognition criteria
findings.description: A trading venue is recognised by the presence of a multilateral system in which multiple third-party buying and selling interests interact under rules in a way that results in a contract. SEA 1934 instead emphasises an organisation that provides a marketplace or facilities for bringing together purchasers and sellers of securities. Discretionary matching distinguishes an OTF from RM/MTF. These are logical tests, not a stored document type.

questions.text: Does this facility operate a multilateral system in which multiple third-party buying and selling interests can interact in the system under its rules so that a contract can result?
answer_data: Boolean plus a short evidence note citing rulebook or authorisation findings.

questions.text: Are interests matched under non-discretionary rules (RM or MTF) or may the operator use discretion (OTF), and is own-account matching of third-party interests prohibited in the way a venue is prohibited from acting as an SI?
answer_data: matching_rule_type in {non-discretionary, discretionary, bilateral-own-account, mixed} and prohibition notes.

questions.text: What observations, with method, time and confidence, distinguish this facility from an adjacent class such as broker crossing, bulletin board, e-commerce catalogue, CCP, or DRSP?
answer_data: Observation object: method, event_time, observation_time, confidence, adjacent_class_rejected, evidence_refs.

questions.text: If the US Exchange Act definition applies, which premises, property rights, communication systems and reporting facilities are included as facilities of this exchange?
answer_data: Array of facility-component descriptions without physical measurements unless a referenced physical-site model supplies them.

data_elements.name: Is multilateral system
data_elements.description: Whether multiple third-party interests interact in-system.

data_elements.name: Matching rule type
data_elements.description: Non-discretionary, discretionary or bilateral.

data_elements.name: Recognition confidence
data_elements.description: Agent confidence in class membership with method and times.

data_elements.name: Exchange Act facility components
data_elements.description: Premises, property rights and communication systems treated as exchange facilities.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Recognition is a set of statutory and ontological tests (multilateral system, non-discretionary versus discretionary rules, bringing together purchasers and sellers, resulting in a contract). The answers are boolean and coded fields plus citations to the authorisation and rulebook artifacts owned by other findings, not a separate stored artefact type.

bundles.name: Legal status and lifecycle
bundles.description: Authorisation or designation of the venue, MIC publication lifecycle, dormancy and vacation, and the operator-location binding that does not own the legal entity.
bundles.rationale: A market exists as a legal facility only while authorised, designated or otherwise permitted, and as a globally identified source of prices only while its MIC is active. CFTC dormancy and ISO expiry are distinct rare lifecycle paths that a record-only model must still represent.

layers.name: Authorisation and MIC lifecycle
layers.description: Licence, designation, suspension, withdrawal, MIC active/updated/expired, and CFTC dormant or vacated states.

findings.name: Authorisation or designation status
findings.description: Regulated markets are authorised under MiFID II Title III; MTFs and OTFs under Title II; US national securities exchanges register with the SEC; DCMs are designated under CEA Section 5 and must observe 23 core principles; SEFs register under CEA Section 5h; MiCA CASPs that operate a trading platform are authorised under Title V. Status is a venue attribute; the act of granting or withdrawing the licence is an authority-owned process.

questions.text: Which competent authority, commission or self-regulatory organisation granted, refused, suspended or withdrew the right to operate this market, and under which statutory provision?
answer_data: authority_name, authority_identifier, statute_citation, act_type in {grant, refuse, suspend, withdraw, reinstate}.

questions.text: What is the current authorisation or designation state of the venue, and on what event-time did that state become effective as distinct from when this record ingested the fact?
answer_data: state in {applied, authorised, designated, suspended, withdrawn, refused, reinstated, unknown}, event_time and observation_time as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

questions.text: Which venue core principles or operating-condition titles apply (for example MiFID Title II or III, CEA 23 DCM principles, 15 SEF principles, MiCA Article 76), without copying the authority's assessment of compliance?
answer_data: Array of applicable principle identifiers and titles; compliance evaluation remains with the authority model.

questions.text: What is the home Member State or home jurisdiction of the market operator, and in which host jurisdictions is the venue passported, notice-registered or otherwise accessible?
answer_data: home_jurisdiction plus array of host_access objects with legal basis.

data_elements.name: Authorising authority
data_elements.description: Identifier and name of the granting authority.

data_elements.name: Authorisation state
data_elements.description: Current legal operating state of the venue.

data_elements.name: Authorisation event time
data_elements.description: Effective time of the current legal state.

data_elements.name: Applicable core principles
data_elements.description: Identifiers of principles the venue must observe.

artifacts.name: Authorisation or designation instrument
artifacts.description: Licence, designation order, Form DCM/SEF equivalent, ESMA or national register extract, or notice of suspension or withdrawal. Evaluation and enforcement case files remain outside this artifact.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing authority, the statutory provision cited and the effective event time of the act.

findings.name: MIC lifecycle and operational dormancy
findings.description: An allocated MIC is never altered and is not removed from the published list; it moves among ACTIVE, UPDATED and EXPIRED. Publication occurs on the second Monday of the month and modifications become effective on the fourth Monday. Separately, a CFTC DCM with no trading for twelve consecutive calendar months is dormant and must reinstate designation; newly designated DCMs have a 36-month grace period; vacated exchanges must reapply. These paths are not the same event.

questions.text: What MIC-status transition is being recorded (creation, update of details, deactivation/expiry), who was entitled to request it, and what are the RA publication date and modification implementation date?
answer_data: transition_type, requester_role, publication_time, implementation_time as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

questions.text: Has trading occurred on this designated contract market in the last twelve consecutive calendar months, is the 36-month new-market grace still running, or has designation been vacated, and at what event-times?
answer_data: Booleans dormant, in_grace, vacated with last_trade_event_time, observation_time and supporting register URL.

questions.text: If this Dimension record is retired, will the MIC be tombstoned rather than hard-deleted, and which adopting-Dimension retention policy executes destruction of any extra local attributes?
answer_data: disposition in {tombstone, expire-in-register, retain}, policy_owner, retain_until.

data_elements.description: creation, update or deactivation.

data_elements.name: RA publication time
data_elements.description: When the MIC list containing the change was published.

data_elements.name: Modification implementation time
data_elements.description: When the MIC change becomes effective.

data_elements.name: Dormant or vacated flag
data_elements.description: CFTC dormancy or vacation state.

findings.inline_only_rationale: MIC status and dormancy are coded lifecycle fields on the register record and designation status. They are not independent document types; supporting notices are captured under authorisation artifacts and the MIC register extract.

layers.name: Operator and location
layers.description: Who manages the market and where it operates, stored as bindings rather than as a copy of the legal-entity or location masters.

findings.name: Operator LEI and operating location
findings.description: ISO 10383 Release 2.0 adds legal entity name and LEI as dedicated fields and records ISO country and city. FIBO models an exchange as a facility that is identified by a MIC, optionally managed by a financial service provider, and that operates in a country and municipality. Market operator under MiFID II may be the regulated market itself.

questions.text: What LEI and legal entity name identify the organisation that operates this market, and is the market operator the same legal person as the market itself?
answer_data: lei (ISO 17442 20-character), legal_entity_name, operator_is_the_market boolean. LEI validity is owned by the legal-entity model.

questions.text: In which ISO country and municipality does this market operate, and does it operate in more than one location?
answer_data: Array of {country_code, municipality, is_primary} using referenced location identifiers.

questions.text: What public website or other official channel is published on the MIC record for this market?
answer_data: URI of the official website or empty if unpublished.

questions.text: What role does the referenced legal person play (market operator, segment operator, reporting-facility operator) without importing that person's corporate lifecycle?
answer_data: Role code plus legal-entity reference only.

data_elements.name: Operator LEI
data_elements.description: ISO 17442 LEI of the operating legal entity.

data_elements.name: Legal entity name
data_elements.description: Name of the operating legal entity on the MIC record.

data_elements.name: Operating country
data_elements.description: ISO country in which the market operates.

data_elements.name: Operating municipality
data_elements.description: City or municipality of operation.

data_elements.name: Official website
data_elements.description: Public website URI.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Operator LEI, legal name, country, city and website are reference fields on the ISO 10383 record and FIBO properties. They bind to legal-entity and location models rather than constituting a standalone operator artefact.

bundles.name: Composition and relationships
bundles.description: Whole-part structure of operating markets and segments, listed instruments as references, and designated post-trade and data-service links that this model does not operate.
bundles.rationale: ISO 10383 requires segment MICs to be linked to an operating MIC. Listing is a venue function over instruments owned elsewhere. Clearing, settlement and trade repositories are PFMI FMIs referenced from the venue, not specialised here.

layers.name: Structure, listings and FMI links
layers.description: Operating-segment tree, facility subtypes, admission-to-trading set, and designated CCP, CSD, SSS, payment and reporting links.

findings.name: Segments, facilities and listed instruments
findings.description: A market-segment MIC identifies a section of an exchange, market or trade-reporting facility that specialises in instruments or is regulated differently and can be registered only if an operating MIC exists. FIBO also specialises auction markets, quote-driven markets, dark pools, off-market/off-book facilities and electronic communication networks. Admission to trading is a venue-side relation to instruments or crypto-assets.

questions.text: Which segment MICs are part of this operating market, and which operating MIC does this segment belong to?
answer_data: Array of child or parent MIC codes with segment purpose notes.

questions.text: Is this facility an auction market, quote-driven market, dark pool, off-book reporting facility, electronic communication network, floor segment, or another specialised facility?
answer_data: Array of FIBO or local facility-subtype codes with evidence.

questions.text: Which referenced instruments, contracts or crypto-assets are admitted to trading or listed under this market's rules, and what is each admission state and effective event-time?
answer_data: Array of {instrument_ref, admission_state, event_time, observation_time}; instrument masters live elsewhere.

questions.text: For a given admitted instrument, is this MIC the place of official listing, a place of trade, both, or neither (reporting-only)?

data_elements.name: Child segment MICs
data_elements.description: Segment identifiers under an operating market.

data_elements.name: Facility subtypes
data_elements.description: Auction, quote-driven, dark, off-book, ECN and similar.

data_elements.name: Admission-to-trading set
data_elements.description: Referenced instruments with admission state.

data_elements.name: Place role
data_elements.description: Listing, trade and/or reporting role of this MIC.

artifacts.name: Venue listing and admission register
artifacts.description: Venue-side register of referenced instruments or contracts admitted, suspended or delisted, with event times. Does not store instrument terms.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the MIC of the admitting market plus the referenced instrument or contract identifier and the admission event time.

findings.name: Post-trade and data-service bindings
findings.description: A venue may designate a CCP, CSD or SSS, a payment arrangement, a trade repository, and data-reporting services. PFMI lifecycle, default management, settlement finality and TR recordkeeping are not specialised in this model. MiFID recital 15 states that CCPs are not OTFs.

questions.text: Which central counterparties, if any, are designated for contracts executed on this market, and what subject-specific parameters (eligible product set, account model) are venue-side only?
answer_data: Array of CCP references plus venue parameters; CCP risk, default and recovery remain in the CCP model.

questions.text: Which CSD, SSS or payment system is designated for settlement of venue trades, and does this venue claim on-chain, off-chain or hybrid settlement initiation without owning settlement finality?
answer_data: csd_ref, sss_ref, payment_system_ref, settlement_mode; finality rules stay with the FMI model.

questions.text: To which trade repository, APA, ARM, CTP or other reporting facility must trades on this market be reported, and which of those destinations have their own MICs?
answer_data: Array of reporting-destination refs and MICs; DRSP operations not owned.

data_elements.name: Designated CCP references
data_elements.description: CCP identifiers bound to this venue.

data_elements.name: Settlement and payment links
data_elements.description: CSD, SSS and payment-system references.

data_elements.name: Reporting destinations
data_elements.description: TR, APA, ARM, CTP or TRF bindings.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are outgoing REFERENCE bindings and subject-specific parameters (which CCP, which TR). The target FMI and DRSP models own lifecycle, evaluation, default management, settlement finality and audit-trail semantics.

bundles.name: Access and operations
bundles.description: Who may use the market, under what access rules, when the market is open, how it publishes transparency, and how it interrupts trading.
bundles.rationale: MiFID II requires transparent and non-discriminatory access rules for trading venues, with OTF-specific ability to restrict access. Venues must manage capacity, co-location on a non-discriminatory basis, and volatility interruptions. CFTC DCMs must publish daily trading information and have emergency authority. These are venue behaviours and affordances, not order-execution ownership.

layers.name: Membership, sessions and transparency
layers.description: Participant classes, fair access, trading calendar, halt state, and pre- and post-trade transparency regime.

findings.name: Membership and fair access
findings.description: Members or participants of RM and MTF are persons admitted under venue rules; the terms are interchangeable in MiFID II and do not include users who only have direct electronic access. SEA 1934 defines exchange members. FIBO defines exchange participant as a registered agent who may trade on or through the exchange. OTFs may restrict access. Co-location must be non-discriminatory, fair and transparent. Fair-access rules also appear in US Regulation ATS.

questions.text: What membership or participant classes exist (member, participant, sponsor, DEA user, retail, eligible contract participant), and which referenced parties currently hold each class without copying those parties' KYC records?
answer_data: Array of class codes and member_refs; party master data remains in the party model.

questions.text: Are access rules transparent, non-discriminatory and based on objective criteria, or does an OTF or other class lawfully restrict access, and where is that stated?
answer_data: access_model in {open-non-discriminatory, restricted-lawful, fair-access-threshold, unknown} plus rule citation.

questions.text: Does the venue offer direct electronic access or co-location, and are those services offered on published non-discriminatory terms?
answer_data: Booleans dea_offered, colocation_offered, non_discriminatory_terms_published, plus terms_ref.

questions.text: Which participants are currently suspended or excluded from trading on this venue, at what event-time, and under which rule, without storing the disciplinary case file?
answer_data: Array of {member_ref, restriction, event_time, rule_cite}; case files stay with the authority or SRO model.

data_elements.name: Participant classes
data_elements.description: Venue-defined membership classes.

data_elements.name: Access model
data_elements.description: Open, restricted or threshold fair-access.

data_elements.name: Direct electronic access offered
data_elements.description: Whether DEA is offered.

data_elements.name: Co-location offered
data_elements.description: Whether co-location is offered on published terms.

artifacts.name: Membership and access rule set
artifacts.description: Venue rules governing admission of members or participants, DEA, co-location and exclusion, as published by the operator.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the MIC of the venue plus the operator's rule reference for admission, DEA, co-location and exclusion.

findings.name: Trading calendar, halts and transparency
findings.description: The venue's operational state includes scheduled sessions, unscheduled halts, volatility interruptions and emergency closures. MiFID II requires venues to be able to halt or constrain trading and to provide pre- and post-trade transparency subject to waivers. CFTC DCMs must publish daily trading information and have emergency authority. Liquidity in the MiFID sense is a measured property of an instrument class on a venue, recorded with method and time, not a physical quantity.

questions.text: What is the trading calendar, session schedule and time zone of this market, and which referenced business-calendar exceptions (holidays, early closes) currently apply?
answer_data: timezone, session_template, exception_refs; holiday masters remain in the calendar model.

questions.text: What is the current operational trading state (scheduled-open, auction, continuous, halted, volatility-interrupt, emergency-closed, ended-for-day) and at what event-time did it start versus when was it observed?
answer_data: state, reason_code, event_time, observation_time as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

questions.text: What pre-trade and post-trade transparency obligations, waivers and deferrals apply to this venue, including dark or delayed publication?

What venue-level activity or liquid-market indicators are recorded (session count, participant count, halt count, declared liquid-market flags for instrument classes), with method, event-time, observation-time and confidence, and without importing order-by-order statistics owned by the trade model?
answer_data: Array of {metric, value, unit, method, event_time, observation_time, confidence}.

questions.text: What matching or execution protocol does the venue advertise (continuous order book, periodic auction, RFQ, quote-driven, hybrid), without claiming ownership of individual match events?
answer_data: Array of protocol codes and applicable segment MICs.

bundles.name: Rules and integrity
bundles.description: The venue rulebook, emergency powers and integrity constraints that bound behaviour of the market as a facility, without owning surveillance evaluation or enforcement cases.
bundles.rationale: Organised markets function in accordance with their rules. CFTC DCM core principles require compliance with rules, prevention of market disruption, emergency authority, disciplinary procedures and system safeguards. MiFID II requires resilient systems, testing and business continuity. Those capabilities and constraints belong to the venue record; investigations and sanctions do not.

layers.name: Rulebook and emergency authority
layers.description: Identified rulebook versions, emergency powers, and system-safeguard claims recorded as venue constraints.

findings.name: Rulebook, governance and emergency powers
findings.description: A market operator must have transparent rules for trading, admission, access and, for DCMs, emergency authority, disciplinary procedures, conflicts of interest, governance fitness, recordkeeping and system safeguards. This finding stores the identity, version and applicability of those rules and the existence of emergency powers. It does not store investigation files, does not execute discipline, and does not evaluate core-principle compliance.

questions.text: What is the current rulebook or operating-rules identifier and version for this market, who issued it, and when did it become effective?
What emergency authorities may the venue exercise (halt, position-limit change, liquidation-only, cancel orders) and what preconditions does the rulebook state, without executing those powers here?
answer_data: Array of emergency-power codes with stated preconditions and reversibility notes.

questions.text: What declared hazards and failure modes does the venue document (disorderly trading, capacity overload, erroneous-order storms, manipulation susceptibility of listed contracts) and what venue-side controls or safe states are claimed?
answer_data: Array of {hazard_or_failure, control, safe_state, evidence_ref}. Surveillance case outcomes remain outside.

questions.text: What recordkeeping and clock-synchronisation obligations apply to this venue as a facility, and which adopting-Dimension or referenced audit model stores the actual audit trail?
answer_data: obligation_summary plus audit_store_owner; this model does not own the audit trail.

bundles.rationale: ISO 10383 exists to facilitate automated processing in any application as place of listing, trade or reporting. Agents must know which register extract they used, when it was published, and which foreign identifiers align without claiming unproven conformance.

findings.name: Public registers and interoperability codes
findings.description: The ISO 10383 list is the global MIC master. ESMA and national registers, SEC exchange and ATS-N filings, and CFTC DCM/SEF lists are jurisdictional masters for legal class. FIBO provides IRIs for market classes. This finding records those evidence sources and any additional identifiers used in messaging, without asserting FIX or ISO 20022 message conformance beyond ISO 10383's stated purpose.

Does not allocate the four-character code

Records alignments without claiming unproven equivalence

composition.purpose: MIC Release 2.0 and FIBO carry LEI and legal entity name of the operator. This model stores the binding and operator-role parameters only and must not reproduce legal-entity identity machinery, control, officers or LEI lifecycle.
Admission to trading and place of official listing are venue-side relations. Instrument identity, terms and lifecycle stay in the instrument model.
MiCA trading platforms admit crypto-assets to trading. The asset, white paper and token lifecycle are not specialised here; only the platform and admission binding are.
The market is a place of trade. Orders, matches, fills and trade state belong to a transaction model. A reference to a matcher or matching protocol is a venue parameter, not ownership of execution.
PFMI treat CCPs as FMIs. MiFID recital 15 excludes CCPs from OTF. This model may name a designated CCP and eligible-product parameters only.

composition.target: Central securities depository / securities settlement system
composition.purpose: CSD and SSS are PFMI FMIs. Settlement finality, accounts and asset servicing are not owned by the venue model.
Money settlement arrangements are PFMI payment systems. The venue may reference them; it does not operate payment-system lifecycle.

composition.target: Trade repository / data reporting services provider
composition.purpose: TRs are PFMI FMIs. APA, ARM and CTP may hold MICs but are reporting services. This model stores destination MICs and reporting obligations only.

Authorisation and core-principle oversight are authority acts. The venue record stores the authority reference and resulting status, not the authority's organisation, investigations or enforcement files.

composition.target: Person or organisation as member or participant
composition.purpose: Membership is a role relative to the exchange. Party identity, fitness and KYC remain in party models; this model stores class, access and restriction parameters.
FIBO requires operates-in-country and operates-in-municipality. Canonical location records stay in the location model.
Session exceptions bind to a calendar master. This model stores the venue template and current exceptions only.
ISO 10383 is the governed global identifier scheme for this subject. Alignment does not by itself confer MiFID, SEA or CEA legal class.

FIBO Exchange, MIC, market category and participant classes are the principal ontology alignment. FIBO treats SI as a subclass of Exchange, which conflicts with MiFID's trading-venue perimeter and must be recorded as a conflict, not silently adopted.

composition.target: MiFID II trading venue (RM, MTF, OTF)
composition.purpose: EU legal classes for multilateral trading venues. Not every MIC is a MiFID trading venue.

composition.target: Securities Exchange Act exchange and Regulation ATS
composition.purpose: US exchange versus ATS exemption is a distinct perimeter from MiFID RM/MTF/OTF.

composition.target: CEA designated contract market and swap execution facility
composition.purpose: US commodity and swap trading facilities with core-principle regimes. Dormancy and vacation are CEA-specific lifecycle paths.
Multilateral crypto-asset platforms are in scope as markets. Crypto-assets that are financial instruments may instead fall under MiFID; the perimeter conflict is recorded, not resolved here.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension owns access policy for owner-gated fields such as member restriction lists, unpublished emergency playbooks and internal halt reasons.
The adopting Dimension owns retention and destruction of extra local attributes not present on the public register, executed only after tombstone, while the MIC identity is retained indefinitely.
The adopting Dimension owns adoption of the proposed REFERENCE and ALIGN links; the registered relations array is empty and those links remain candidate composition, not adopted contracts.
The adopting Dimension owns exception execution and the outstanding cross-jurisdiction multi-profile validation.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Registry entry vr.wm-eco-001 under model WM-ECO-001. Instance identity uses the ISO 10383 MIC namespace at operating (OPRT) and segment (SGMT) level; a Dimension UUID or ULID is used only until a MIC is allocated, and the operator LEI is kept as a referenced legal-entity identifier rather than a market identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity is the four-character ISO 10383 MIC matching [A-Z0-9]{4}; the operator LEI is a reference and is not the market identifier.
ISO 10383 publication date and modification implementation date are distinct event times and must not be collapsed into ingestion time.
Segment records canonically carry both their own MIC and the operating MIC, which are equal when the record is operating-level.
patch_rules: MIC characters are immutable once allocated; patches may change only names, category, LEI binding, status, location, listings, access rules and trading state.
Segment links must remain consistent with an existing operating MIC.
Do not overwrite jurisdictional legal class solely because the ISO 10383 market category changed.
Differences found against the current MIC publication are recorded as evidence rather than applied as a silent overwrite of legal-class fields owned by jurisdictional registers.
compatibility_rules: Treat ISO 10383, MiFID II, SEA 1934, CEA and MiCA classes as alignments and fail closed on silent conformance claims.
SI and DRSP records that carry MICs must not be classified as MiFID trading venues.
FIX tag 30 LastMkt and ISO 20022 PlaceOfTrade bindings are interoperability holds, not claimed mappings.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) assigned and published by SWIFT as the ISO 10383 Registration Authority
governed global identifier or IRI such as a FIBO market individual IRI; the operator LEI is a referenced legal-entity identifier and is not the market identifier
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only when no MIC yet exists and replaced when a MIC is allocated
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when the MIC change, authorisation act, listing, halt or session transition occurred or became effective) separately from observation or ingestion time when those differ. ISO 10383 publication date and modification implementation date are distinct event times and must not be collapsed into ingestion time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by the venue MIC plus the event time of the instance: MIC register records by the publication and modification implementation dates of the list used; rulebooks by rulebook identifier plus version and effective event time; calendar and halt notices by MIC plus the notice event time; register extract packs by register name, source URL and publication time.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: An identified market record is never hard-deleted: ISO 10383 never removes an allocated MIC from the published list, the code is set to EXPIRED with an expiry date and remains a historical identifier, and local records tombstone while retaining the MIC. Every artifact carries source_refs and both event time and observation time.

policies: Validation: Validate MIC pattern [A-Z0-9]{4}, MIC type against operating MIC, status against {ACTIVE, UPDATED, EXPIRED}, LEI format if present, and that SI/DRSP records are not classified as MiFID trading venues. Treat ISO, MiFID, SEA, CEA and MiCA classes as alignments and fail closed on silent conformance claims.

Retention: Retain expired MIC identity indefinitely as a historical place-of-trade key. Retain listing and trading-state history for the period required by venue recordkeeping rules and adopting-Dimension policy. Destruction of extra local attributes, if any, is executed by adopting-Dimension policy after tombstone; referenced models own destruction of operator, trade and audit records.

read: Project public register fields by default.
Owner-gated fields (member restriction lists, unpublished emergency playbooks, internal halt reasons) require adopting-Dimension access policy.
create: Populate from an ISO 10383 extract and, where applicable, a jurisdictional register or authorisation artifact.
Do not mint a four-character MIC locally; request allocation from the Registration Authority.
A Dimension UUID or ULID may hold a pre-MIC draft.
Pre-write checks: unique MIC, OPRT/SGMT consistency with operating MIC, LEI treated as a reference, no date used as identifier.
Post-write checks: source_refs present, event time and observation time both set.
update: MIC characters are immutable once allocated.
Updates may change names, category, LEI binding, status, location, listings, access rules and trading state.
Segment links must remain consistent with an existing operating MIC.
Do not overwrite jurisdictional legal class solely because ISO category changed.
delete: Do not hard-delete an identified market record.
ISO 10383 never removes an allocated MIC from the published list; the code is set to EXPIRED with an expiry date and remains a historical identifier.

Local Dimension records must tombstone or mark expired, retain the MIC, and apply adopting-Dimension retention and destruction policy only to extra local attributes not present on the public register.

Execution of operator-entity dissolution is owned by the legal-entity model; execution of licence withdrawal is owned by the competent-authority model; execution of trade, order and audit-trail deletion is owned by those referenced models or by adopting-Dimension policy when no such model is bound.

roles.name: ISO 10383 Registration Authority (SWIFT SC)
responsibilities: Allocates the four-character non-intelligent MIC and never modifies an allocated code.
Publishes the MIC list on the second Monday of the month with modifications effective on the fourth Monday.
Maintains MIC status ACTIVE, UPDATED or EXPIRED and never removes an allocated code from the published list.

roles.name: Market operator
responsibilities: Operates the market or segment in accordance with its published rulebook.
Publishes access, direct-electronic-access and co-location terms on non-discriminatory, fair and transparent conditions.
Maintains the admission-to-trading set and declares trading state, halts, volatility interruptions and emergency closures.

roles.name: Competent authority, commission or self-regulatory organisation
responsibilities: Grants, refuses, suspends, withdraws or reinstates the right to operate the market under a stated statutory provision.
Owns core-principle assessment, supervisory evaluation, disciplinary case files and enforcement records, which this model does not store.

roles.name: Adopting Dimension steward
responsibilities: Ingests register extracts and records register provenance with publication, implementation, ingestion times and ingesting actor.
Applies access, retention and destruction policy to owner-gated fields and to extra local attributes after tombstone.
Decides adoption of the candidate REFERENCE and ALIGN links, which are not adopted contracts by default.

roles.name: Member or participant
responsibilities: Is admitted under venue rules as a member or participant; users holding only direct electronic access are not members.
May trade on or through the exchange subject to the venue access rules and current restrictions.

access.default_rule: Public ISO 10383 fields are minimum-disclosure and are projected by default.
exceptions: Authorisation instruments, member registers, unpublished halt reasons and emergency playbooks are owner-gated under adopting-Dimension policy.
This model does not grant access to FMI, trade or surveillance stores by reference.
Minimum-disclosure projection uses de-disclosure-class to split public register data from owner-gated operating detail.
audit_requirements: Record register provenance for each populated record: register name, source URL, publication time, implementation time, ingested_at and ingested_by.
Record event time separately from observation or ingestion time for MIC changes, authorisation acts, listings, halts and session transitions, using RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.
Venue recordkeeping and clock-synchronisation obligations are stored as constraints only; the audit trail itself is owned by the referenced audit model or by adopting-Dimension policy.

coverage.claim: This pass covers ISO 10383 MIC identity together with EU MiFID II and MiCA and US SEA and CEA venue classes as the densest primary regimes; no canonical completeness claim is permitted, and other national licensing regimes, energy and spot marketplaces, and message-binding specifications remain outstanding.

Applicability required. Non-physical properties only: names, class, status, protocols, transparency regime, access model. No geometry, mass, material or colour.
Applicability required. Multilateral-system test, adjacent-class rejection, register evidence, confidence, method and times.

checklist.dimension: five-facet: capabilities, behaviour and possible actions
checklist.notes: Applicability required. Capability: bring together interests, admit instruments, halt trading, publish transparency. Behaviour: non-discretionary or discretionary matching under stated conditions. State and transition: authorisation and trading states. Affordance: members may trade; authorities may designate. Operation: record, classify, bind, validate, tombstone. Constraint: access rules, waivers, MIC immutability. Hazard and failure mode: disorderly trading and capacity overload with claimed safe states; evaluation and enforcement not owned.
Applicability required. Operator, authority, location, calendar, register provenance, disclosure class and master-system extract.

known_omissions: National exchange-licensing regimes outside the EU, US federal CEA/SEA and MiCA (for example Japan FIEA, Hong Kong SFO, MAS, SEBI, CVM, CSRC) were not fetched as primary texts and are unmarked as canonical classes.

Wholesale energy organised marketplaces under REMIT, agricultural spot exchanges, warehouse-receipt markets and spectrum or treasury auction systems lack primary support in this pass and may be sibling models.

FIX tag 30 LastMkt and ISO 20022 PlaceOfTrade message bindings are implied by ISO 10383's purpose but were not fetched as first-party technical specifications; they are interoperability holds, not claimed mappings.
WFE membership, IOSCO Objectives and Principles for secondary-market regulation, and EU DLT Pilot Regime (Regulation 2022/858) trading venues were not ingested as primary sources.
Tick-size, lot-size, colocation fee schedules and market-data licensing products are likely omitted and may belong to fee or data-product siblings.
Whether APA/ARM/CTP should ever be instantiated as WM-ECO-001 records remains unresolved; they have MICs but are not markets.
Islamic capital-market exchanges, SME growth-market subclass operational detail, security-futures dual CFTC/SEC notice registration workflows, and national ATS/MTF subtypes beyond those named.
Market-maker scheme agreements required by MiFID recital 113 are referenced only as a constraint, not modelled as contracts.
Clock synchronisation to UTC as a technical standard (MiFID RTS 25) was not fetched.
Unresolved boundary: Systematic internaliser is MIC-bearing in ISO 10383/FIBO but is not a trading venue under MiFID Article 4(24); instantiation policy is a Dimension choice.
Unresolved boundary: DRSPs with MICs versus a dedicated data-reporting model.
Unresolved boundary: Physical marketplace or bazaar without a MIC.
Unresolved boundary: Prediction markets and event-contract venues where CEA versus CFTC jurisdiction is contested.
Unresolved boundary: When a crypto-asset platform is a MiCA CASP versus a MiFID trading venue because the token is a financial instrument.
conflicts: MiFID II Article 4(24) trading venue equals RM, MTF or OTF only; ISO 10383 and FIBO assign MICs and Exchange subclasses to SI, DRSP and CASP.
FIBO uses market as a synonym of exchange; competition-law relevant market is a different neighbour.
SEA 1934 exchange includes ATS-like systems that may operate under an exemption rather than as a national securities exchange.
PFMI FMI set excludes trading venues; some operators are vertically integrated with CCP or CSD legal persons and must still be split across models.
regional_assumptions: Legal class enumerations are written against EU MiFID II/MiCA and US SEA/CEA as the densest primary regimes. Other jurisdictions must be added as profiles, not assumed to match.
CFTC dormancy (twelve months, 36-month grace, vacated reapplication) is US DCM-specific and must not be generalised to every exchange.
ISO 10383 publication on the second Monday and effectiveness on the fourth Monday follow the RA's Belgian calendar.
